title: Chapter 10
content:
Tossing and turning, Jakyeong was jolted awake by the thumping beat of music leaking in from outside. A quick glance at his wristwatch told him it was 10:00 AM.

He dragged his stiff, achy body upright and rubbed the sleep from his face. High above, the ceiling camera was still blinking its little red light, faithfully recording his every twitch. Might as well be living in a five-star prison.

Swinging his legs out of bed, he padded into the private lounge. He wondered what maniac was blasting tunes this early in the morning, only to spot the back of a head sticking up over the sofa cushions. Kang Il-hyun? No, ear-splitting EDM didn't seem like the stoic hitman-in-a-suit's style.

"Excuse me... who are you?"

The man on the sofa whipped his head around. Reaching for his phone, he cut the music and stood up.

He was surprisingly tall, sporting dark sunglasses and a sharp, haughty aura that bore an uncanny resemblance to Kang Il-hyun. Even without an introduction, Jakyeong immediately knew who this was: the younger brother Il-hyun had mentioned yesterday.

"You're finally up?" the man drawled, completely skipping any polite greetings. "You were sleeping so late, I was debating whether to wake you."

Debating? You were blasting music loud enough to rupture eardrums. Why didn't you just march into the bedroom and shake me by the skull? The snarky retort surged right to the tip of Jakyeong’s tongue, but he swallowed it down.

"Go wash up," the man ordered casually, dropping straight into informal speech. "We have places to be."

"Where... are we going?"

"Second Brother told me to take you to an art exhibition."

Seeing the sour, reluctant twist of the kid's mouth, it was obvious Il-hyun had forced this errand on him. Jakyeong’s mental dossier on the kid was simple: twenty-one years old, son of the third wife, a chronic junkie, and an unhinged party animal.

Sure enough, the guy kept sniffing incessantly—a telltale twitch that looked all too familiar to Jakyeong.

"And drop the honorifics with me," Kang Seok-joo added flippantly. "We're the same age."

Without waiting for a reply, Seok-joo dropped back onto the sofa and blasted his deafening playlist again. Sensing that another word would only trigger a tantrum, Jakyeong slipped back into his suite.

He popped a nicotine-suppressant pill, stepped into the shower, and let the hot water wash away the lingering morning grogginess.

After toweling off and drying his hair, he threw on his change of clothes. Having to change inside a steamy bathroom just to avoid a damn security camera is absurd. Standing before the mirror, he slipped on his black horn-rimmed glasses. The specs were tolerable, but this prim, navy plaid button-down felt utterly foreign. It was the exact opposite of his usual style.

Shaking his head, he walked out to the bedroom and strapped on his luxury watch. He’d bought a few absurdly expensive accessories purely to play the part of a pampered young heir. The moment this contract was fulfilled, he planned to pawn every single piece. Not a single item in his wardrobe suited his taste.

When he emerged into the lounge, Seok-joo was slouched with his feet kicked up on the coffee table. Seeing Jakyeong, he pushed himself up, and the two headed downstairs together.

Kang Il-hyun was nowhere in sight. According to the elderly housekeeper, he’d rushed out at the crack of dawn on urgent company business. Taking note of Jakyeong's offhand comment that he wasn't a big fan of heavy rice dishes in the morning, the sweet woman had prepared a fresh plate of toasted bread and crisp garden salad instead.

While Jakyeong ate, Seok-joo slumped in the opposite chair, fiercely glued to a mobile game on his phone. Above the dark rims of his sunglasses, his brows twitched continuously. Whenever a round went south, low curses slipped out between his teeth.

Sipping the freshly squeezed juice the housekeeper had made, Jakyeong quietly observed the kid. The way Seok-joo relentlessly gnawed on his bottom lip reeked of classic withdrawal anxiety.

"What are you staring at?"

Jakyeong thought the kid was lost in his screen, but apparently not. With a piece of toast still tucked in his mouth, Jakyeong managed a meek, harmless smile.

Just as he was finishing up his plate, footsteps echoed from the front entryway. Who could that be at this hour?Jakyeong leaned his head back against the chair to look—and to his utter surprise, Kang Il-hyun came striding into the dining room. Wait. Didn't the maid say he left for work at dawn?

"Executive Director Kang," the housekeeper greeted warmly.

The second the title dropped, Seok-joo jammed his phone into his pocket and shot up from his seat like a spring. Jakyeong could feel the kid's entire nervous system snap taut in an instant. Seok-joo ripped off his sunglasses, dropped his head low, and bowed with trembling deference.

"You're back, Brother..."

Il-hyun didn't even acknowledge the greeting. Instead, he pulled out the chair directly beside Jakyeong and sat down.

Seok-joo eased back into his seat, watching Il-hyun's face with terror-stricken eyes. The swaggering, arrogant delinquent from ten minutes ago was nowhere to be found.

Jakyeong set down his toast and picked up his juice glass. Having this lethal apex predator suddenly drop into the adjacent chair made his breakfast feel like lead in his stomach.

Fortunately, the housekeeper stepped in, softening the stifling tension. "You're back early, Executive Director. Barely two hours."

"I left something in my study," Il-hyun replied smoothly. "Could you brew me a cup of coffee, please?"

As he spoke, Il-hyun casually draped his right arm along the back of Jakyeong’s chair.

Feeling the warmth of that heavy arm resting just behind his shoulder blades, Jakyeong deliberately straightened his spine, pulling forward to create some distance.

Noticing the shift, Il-hyun turned his head, his dark eyes locking onto Jakyeong's face.

"Did you sleep well?"

Uncomfortable as hell. Swallowing down the food in his mouth, Jakyeong gave a timid, docile nod. "Yes... thanks to your hospitality..."

Il-hyun’s piercing gaze drifted across the table, settling on his younger brother. "Have you two properly introduced yourselves?"

Seok-joo fidgeted like a restless dog that needed to be let out. "Yes, Brother..."

With his sunglasses off, Seok-joo’s face bore an undeniable resemblance to Il-hyun's, but the aura behind the eyes was worlds apart. Where Il-hyun projected absolute, lethal dominance, Seok-joo looked like a terrified schoolboy cowering before a tyrannical principal. And right across his temple was a raw, angry scar—a violent souvenir from their encounter two nights ago.

The housekeeper returned with a steaming mug of black coffee. Il-hyun picked it up and stood from the table, but as he did, his hand moved from the chair back to rest firmly on Jakyeong’s shoulder.

The sudden physical contact sent an electric jolt through Jakyeong's body, causing him to stiffen.

"Kang Seok-joo."

Seok-joo’s head snapped up as if he’d been scorched with a hot iron. "Yes, Brother?"

"Look after Yi-an today. Make sure he's well taken care of."

"Understood... Brother."

Hearing a twenty-one-year-old punk address his older brother with such stiff, subservient honorifics was almost comical. It spoke volumes about how terrifying the family dynamic really was.

The heavy hand lifted away from Jakyeong’s shoulder. Dropping a casual line wishing them a pleasant day, Il-hyun turned and disappeared down the inner hallway with his coffee.

Jakyeong rolled his shoulder slightly, shaking off the phantom heat of Il-hyun's touch. As he let out a quiet breath, his eyes met Seok-joo's across the table. For a split second, an unspoken spark of mutual understanding passed between them.

The look in the kid's eyes said it all:

You hate that psycho bastard too, don't you?

A toddler could paint better than this with their feet, Jakyeong thought dryly, staring blankly at the incomprehensible modern canvas before him.

The painting depicted a bizarre human portrait with a pair of wide eyes painted directly onto the back of the subject's skull. What was the artist trying to say? Watch your back so you don't get stabbed? If that was the message, Jakyeong was half-tempted to buy the damn piece and hang it in his bedroom. In his line of work, trusting no one was a rule drilled into your skull from day one.

He had spent the entire afternoon trailing after Kang Seok-joo. They’d browsed boutique galleries in Insadong, picked up a few useless souvenirs, and by sunset, arrived at the private art museum operated by Haewon Group. After hours of looking at canvases, Jakyeong’s utter lack of art appreciation had evolved into sheer boredom.

He almost felt bad for the young deputy director who was passionately explaining the concepts behind every piece. Since Jakyeong had lied about being a fine arts major, he had to play along, offering a hollow barrage of nodding and deadpan compliments: "Fascinating. Incredible. Absolutely stunning."

"Honestly, I could draw better than this using my left foot."

Jakyeong turned his head at the sudden voice. Having returned from the restroom, Seok-joo chimed in, unloading his unfiltered disdain for the artwork. He scoffed that a finger-painting from his kindergarten days had more artistic value, loudly questioning what kind of moron would spend actual money on this garbage.

With every vicious quip, the polite smile on the deputy director’s face steadily dissolved.

"How much?" Seok-joo asked abruptly.

The woman forced a strained, professional smile. "For the painting, sir?"

"No. To sleep with you."

"Excuse me?!"

"Don't play dumb," Seok-joo sneered, looking her up and down. "It's pathetic."

A burning flush crept up the woman’s neck and ears. Mercifully, a gallery staff member hurried over, whispering that an urgent call had come in for her. Masking her humiliation behind a crisp, professional bow, she quickly excused herself and walked away.

Seok-joo licked his lips openly as he watched her retreat. "Looks tasty, doesn't she?"

When Jakyeong didn't respond, Seok-joo raised his pinky finger and gave it a suggestive wag. "She’s Kang Tae-han's side piece. You know Tae-han, right? My eldest brother. There's a reason a girl that young got handed the deputy director title here so easily."

"..."

"Maybe I should ask him to share?"

"..."

"Why are you looking at me like that? Does this kind of talk make you blush, little virgin?"

You're the one acting like a shameless degenerate, so why the hell are you asking if I'm embarrassed? If this kid were one of his peers back in the slums, Jakyeong would have caved the back of his skull in until his eyeballs popped out.

Just then, Seok-joo’s phone began blaring. He answered it right beside Jakyeong, the caller’s voice booming through the speaker so loud it echoed against the gallery walls. Seok-joo didn't even bother turning the volume down.

"You deaf piece of shit, how many times do I have to tell you? I said I can't come!"

[Why not?]

"We have a guest staying at my house, and I was told to babysit him."

[What guest? A chick?]

"Shut the fuck up, moron. It's a guy."

[Even better! Bring him along! Choi Ki-tae said he’s bringing the good shit tonight.]

The annoyance on Seok-joo’s face vanished, replaced by an instant, hungry glint. His eyes snapped toward Jakyeong, who had drifted a few steps away to pretend to study another piece.

After a beat of hesitation, Seok-joo hung up and called out: "Hey... what was your name again?"

We’ve been together all damn day and you still can't remember three syllables? Jakyeong marveled at the sheer stupidity. Whether the kid’s brain had rotted from excessive narcotics or he was simply born an idiot was an open question.

"Jang Yi-an."

"Right, Yi-an. Do you really need to look at more of these paintings?"

"Why...?"

"I have to meet up with some friends real quick. Want to come with?"

"Right now?"

"Yeah. You just have to sit there for a bit."

"..."

"Just... don't tell my second brother about this."

"..."

When Jakyeong didn't immediately jump at the offer, Seok-joo's expression soured into anxious impatience. Seeing Jakyeong keep his mouth shut, Seok-joo unclasped the heavy luxury watch from his wrist and shoved it into Jakyeong’s chest. It was a high-end Swiss masterpiece easily worth over a hundred thousand dollars. Tossing it over like a treat to a stray dog was peak chaebol arrogance.

"Hush money," Seok-joo said flatly. "Keep your mouth shut."

Jakyeong stared at the luxury timepiece, then slowly nodded his head. If you're practically begging to hand over free cash, who am I to refuse? Besides, pretending to appreciate modern art was rapidly driving him insane anyway.

The moment Jakyeong pocketed the watch, Seok-joo let out a satisfied grin and clapped him on the shoulder.

"Let's move."

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • The Pinky Finger Gesture (새끼손가락): In South Korea, raising a pinky finger is a common, slightly crude hand gesture denoting a "mistress," "girlfriend," or "side piece." Seok-joo uses it here to explicitly out the deputy director as his eldest brother's concubine.

  • Informal Speech / Banmal (말 놓다): Seok-joo immediately telling Jakyeong to drop honorifics reflects how Korean peers of the exact same age (both 21) typically interact casually, though Seok-joo's one-sided lack of manners underscores his spoiled upbringing.

  • Chaebol Watch / "A Hundred Million Won" (억은 족히 넘는): 100,000,000 KRW is roughly $75,000 - $85,000 USD. Casual bribery with luxury timepieces illustrates the astronomical, detached wealth of the Kang family.
